title: Had you been harsh
hookLine: by Allah's mercy he was gentle; had he been harsh they'd have left, so consult them (3:159)

cards: Before Uhud, the Prophet ﷺ held a meeting. Should they stay inside Medina and defend the streets, or march out to meet the army in the open? He leaned toward staying.
Many of the younger men, eager to fight, wanted to go out. He listened, and he went out with them. And you know how it ended.
The advice you might expect next: stop asking them. You know better. The Qur'an says the opposite.

teach.b: Here's 3:159 in Pickthall's words: "It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them (O Muhammad), for if thou hadst been stern and fierce of heart they would have dispersed from round about thee."
Then: so pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult with them in the affair. And when you've decided, put your trust in God. Look at the order.
First, gentleness is called a mercy from God, not a weakness.
Second, the people around the Prophet would have scattered if he'd been harsh; the verse says so plainly, about the Prophet himself.
Third, right after a decision made by consultation went badly, the command is: keep consulting.

The word is shawirhum, consult them, from the same root as shura, consultation. The forty-second surah is called ash-Shura, and 42:38 describes believers as people whose affairs are settled by counsel among themselves.
Scholars have long debated how binding consultation is on a leader, and what form it takes, from a ruler's council to a family deciding where to live. But the core is simple. Ask the people affected.
Then decide, and trust God with the outcome, without second-guessing forever. One more detail.

teach.h: HAD YOU BEEN HARSH, THEY WOULD HAVE LEFT.
teach.b: The Prophet, Muslims believe, received revelation; if anyone could have skipped the meeting, it was him.
Yet at Hudaybiyyah, Sahih al-Bukhari reports, when his companions hesitated, he took the advice of his wife Umm Salamah, and it worked.

how: Muslims treat shura, consultation, as a principle for families, mosques and communities; mosque committees, family decisions and Islamic political thought all draw on 3:159 and 42:38, with differing views on how binding consultation is.

o: a vote where the majority always wins
a ruling given by one leader alone

s: after Uhud, the Qur'an told the Prophet to stop consulting
3:159 says consult them in the affair, right after the loss.
the verse calls the Prophet's gentleness a mercy from God
it was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them.
scholars all agree on how binding shura is
they have long debated its force and its form.

games.q: you're leading a group. you asked their advice, followed it, and it went badly. what does 3:159 tell the Prophet in that very moment?
o: pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them.
find out who gave the bad advice.
games.why: pardon, forgiveness, and more consultation. then, once decided, trust in God.

practice: Think of a decision in front of you that touches someone else, at home, at work, in the family, and picture the person it affects most.
Ask yourself honestly whether you've asked them, then imagine the conversation, and yourself listening gently, not waiting for your turn to speak.

wordCard.voice: Shura. Consultation, deciding together by counsel. From 3:159, consult them in the affair, and from the surah named after it. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: consultation, counsel (42:38); 3:159 uses the verb shawirhum, consult them.

carryVoice: Your line: gentle, and consult. In this verse, gentleness is a mercy, not a weakness. That's day three hundred seventy-three.

sources.q: It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them (O Muhammad), for if thou hadst been stern and fierce of heart they would have dispersed from round about thee.
